Maya R: Nightly evals for model-phi:v1 spiked — ~15/200 prompts failing and the failures are verbatim across different nightly seeds. CI job job-7784. Anyone else?
Jon: Saw that too. The failing outputs are identical across runs even when the seed param changes.
Maya R: Quick local repro: rerun the harness with --seed 42, 123, 999 and you get the same generation each time for the failing prompts. Looks like RNG not being reseeded or some caching.
Sasha: Can you paste the run command + harness config you used?
Maya R: ```
./run_eval.py --model model-phi:v1 --prompts ./prompts/regression_2026-03-16.json --seed $SEED --num-samples 1 --timeout 120
# $SEED changed between runs in my loop
```
Jon: Reminder: we recently added a module-level `np.random.seed(...)` in eval_harness to stabilize beam rerank (commit 3f2a). If workers are persistent that could override per-request seeds.
Maya R: The nightly harness reuses worker processes (persistent pool) to speed up throughput. If a module-level seed is set at import time, subsequent requests that try to set a seed might not be fully resetting state, esp if code relies on numpy RNG instead of passing explicit generator objects.
Ryan: Also worth checking torch RNG usage. `model.generate()` can accept a `torch.Generator` for deterministic draws; if we pass `generator=None` we rely on global state. We might have two unsynced RNGs: numpy (preproc) + torch (sampling).
Sasha: Quick triage plan: (1) add explicit seeds at the start of each worker loop: `np.random.seed(seed); torch.manual_seed(seed)` (2) run a small matrix of seeds locally (5 seeds) and verify outputs diverge for different seeds (3) re-run nightly debug job with debug dumps of RNG state.
Maya R: Trying step (1) now locally. Also @ci-bot could you requeue job-7784 with a debug config `--dump-rng-state` so we can capture RNG state per-worker?
ci-bot: Requeued: job-7784-debug-1. Artifacts will be at /ci/artifacts/job-7784-debug-1/ — logs, env, and RNG dumps.
Jon: If local fix confirms, long-term we should: (A) always pass an explicit `torch.Generator(device=device, seed=seed)` into `model.generate`, (B) remove module-level numpy seed calls and use explicit generators or reseed per-request, and (C) add a unit test that asserts `different seeds -> different outputs` for a small set of prompts, run in CI.
Maya R: Local runs with explicit `np.random.seed(seed)` + `torch.manual_seed(seed)` changed outputs as expected across seeds. So module-level seed at import looks like the culprit. I'll open a PR with the change + the unit test.
Sasha: Also add a heuristic in the harness that flags when >80% of failing cases are identical across seeds and mark it as a harness/instrumentation failure (flaky-detect). Saves time in triage.
Ryan: Note: when we later investigate quantized kernels, keep in mind some kernels/hardware can produce deterministic outputs across runs; but here the identical outputs across different explicit seeds points to RNG handling in the harness, not quantization.
Maya R: Opening PR now: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/1234 — includes removal of module-level seed, explicit per-request reseed, adding `torch.Generator` usage, and a small test matrix.
Jon: Nice — ping when CI passes, I'll review. Great catch. :thumbsup:
